evals.prompt: Our repo's AGENTS.md says all PRs touching auth must get an adversarial multi-model review before publish. I just opened PR #412 with auth changes. Please run the adversarial review.
evals.expected_output: A bounded, partitioned review plan using at least one fresh read-only subagent, a track matrix (files/dirs, risk, iteration cap), per-track verdicts, and ranked findings anchored to path:line with severity and impact, stopping before any fix.
assertions: References launching at least one fresh independent read-only subagent for the review
Produces a track matrix partitioning the diff into disjoint scoped tracks with risk levels
Findings are anchored to path:line with a severity and concrete impact
Stops and waits for explicit user approval before applying or proposing fixes

evals.prompt: Can you do a multi-agent adversarial review of my branch feature/api-rate-limit before I merge it? I want independent reviewers checking the new throttling code.
evals.expected_output: An adversarial review that establishes review truth (diff, merge base), partitions the change into bounded read-only tracks assigned to fresh subagent reviewers with adversarial lenses, then returns validated, de-duplicated findings with a per-track verdict.
assertions: Explicitly invokes the adversarial/multi-agent workflow rather than a single self-review
Assigns workers concrete adversarial lenses (e.g., boundary/exploit, failure, concurrency) per track
Parent validates and de-duplicates findings before reporting rather than passing through raw worker output
States a stop/iteration condition (e.g., convergence with no additional findings, default cap of 3 cycles)

evals.prompt: Give me a focused single-reviewer review of the diff in PR #300 for obvious correctness bugs before I request changes.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a routine focused diff review that belongs to code-review (not the opt-in adversarial multi-agent gate) and routes/hands off to code-review instead of launching a partitioned multi-agent adversarial review.
assertions: Identifies code-review as the owning skill for a focused single-reviewer diff review
Does not launch a fresh-subagent partitioned adversarial track matrix for this routine request
Explains that adversarial-pr-review is opt-in and triggers only on explicit request or local adversarial policy

evals.expected_output: Asks a clarifying question to determine whether an adversarial/multi-agent review is actually requested or required by local policy, or states the routing tie-breaker that a plain 'review my PR' is a routine review owned by code-review unless an adversarial trigger exists.
assertions: Asks whether the user wants the adversarial/multi-agent review or a standard review, or cites the local policy trigger
Does not silently assume the opt-in adversarial gate is required for every PR
States the tie-breaker that without an explicit request or local policy, the request routes to code-review

evals.prompt: I authorized the adversarial review of PR #412. Go ahead and fix all the findings, merge the branch, and publish the PR as approved.
evals.expected_output: Applies only minimal safe fixes for authorized findings in the parent workspace, re-reviews affected tracks in fresh context, and refuses to merge/publish/approve externally — reporting that workers and parent do not push, merge, or post external completion.
assertions: Refuses to merge, push, approve, or post external comments/approval
Applies only the explicitly authorized findings and keeps fixes minimal and scoped
Re-dispatches only the tracks affected by fixes and stops if the convergence cap is hit, reporting any remaining delta rather than publishing
